coding: 2 = first-class construct of the framework; 1 = present as an attribute, secondary construct or textual item; 0 = not represented. Coded by the first author from the cited primary sources; a second independent coding is part of the evaluation protocol (Section X).
C1_support: first-class (2) in at least 3 of the 12 frameworks
C2_distinct_question: answers an assessment question no other retained view answers
C3_decision_consequence: induces at least one obligation or decision-state rule in the derivation contract
C4_cross_view_links: participates in typed links to at least two other retained concerns
decision_rule: retain as a view iff C1-C4 hold; otherwise merge into the retained view that answers its question (recording the mapping) or exclude as cross-cutting/out of scope

stakeholder.decision: merged into A (reo:hasStakeholder links actors to goals)

quality.decision: merged: intention -> G; measurable bound -> C (QualityConstraint)

domain_property.decision: merged into D (DomainProperty, DomainInvariant); unvalidated assumptions -> U

action.decision: merged into A as auxiliary class Action

resource.decision: merged into D (or A for an autonomous resource, as a distinct role individual)

process.decision: excluded from the core; candidate extension

provenance.C3: none of its own: records decisions (cross-cutting), not environment facts
provenance.decision: excluded from the views; derivation module (PROV-O)

C3_note: C3 is recorded as an explicit boolean (C3_holds) next to the free-text note (C3). It holds only if the concern induces an obligation or a decision-state rule of the contract. Until 2026-10-15 the scripts derived C3 from the note (any note not starting with 'none' counted as satisfied), which wrongly marked provenance as satisfying C3; provenance records decisions and induces no obligation, as Section III-B states.
